root_idea.summary: Something generated from something else and gathered or formed, especially produce or fruit.
root_idea.development: The concrete sense of fruit extends to fruit-bearing, increase and wealth, benefit or result, and several figurative extensions based on resemblance in form or productive outcome. Some conventional extensions, such as the full-moon expression, are lexically exceptional.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَثْمَرَ.
Displayed under the common nominal citation form ثَمَر.
The Quranic plural ثَمَرَات is presented under the singular/collective nominal citation form ثَمَر.
The singulative ثَمَرَة is presented under the common nominal citation form ثَمَر.

senses.definition: To put forth, bear, or produce fruit.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of a tree or other fruit-bearing thing; the Quranic occurrences express the general fruit-bearing event without specifying a separate ripeness stage.

senses.definition: Fruit or produce of trees, whether eaten or not.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes the collective or uncountable noun ثَمَر, its plural ثَمَرَات, and the singulative ثَمَرَة as represented by the merged Quranic form groups.

senses.definition: Accumulated or acquired property and wealth.
senses.usage_conditions: Reported as an interpretation of ثَمَر in a Quranic passage, alongside the concrete fruit sense; the interpretation is especially associated with the passage at 18:34 in the Quran-focused lexical discussion.
An attributed Quranic interpretation in the lexical tradition, explicitly noted as not being ordinary usage in the proper language; no modern verse location is assigned to the historical citation.
An attributed interpretation of the plural ثَمَرَات in a Quranic passage, distinct from the ordinary concrete fruit reading; no modern verse location is assigned to the historical citation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become ripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of fruit or produce reaching ripeness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect trees or shrubs for sheep or goats.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become abundant in wealth or to possess increasing wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intransitive use concerning a person's property or resources.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant, to shed its blossoms and set, organize, or compact its fruit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes the formation and consolidation of fruit after flowering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show the incipient formation of butter in milk; or, of milk, to have formed visible butter clots before they collect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized dairy use referring to the early coagulation or appearance of butter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make wealth abundant or to increase and develop it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative or transitive use concerning property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter or reach the fruit-bearing stage, including putting forth fruit that may be unripe or ripe or reaching the time for plucking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical accounts distinguish among beginning to fruit, producing unripe or ripe fruit, and reaching the stage at which fruit can be gathered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become abundant in wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use applied to a person rather than to a fruit-bearing plant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiomatic expression, to continue or endure indefinitely.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Restricted to the conventional expression recorded in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feed a person with fruits.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive food-related use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tree or shrub.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use in which ثَمَرَة denotes an individual tree or shrub rather than its produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Offspring or progeny; in an idiom, procreative capacity or sexual appetite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The offspring sense is extended in the recorded expression to a person's ability or desire to procreate or engage in sexual intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The profit, benefit, or resulting good of something, including an increase in property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative result language may describe the benefit of knowledge, good works, or another activity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The knot or terminal appendage of a whip.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension based on the form and hanging of fruit from a tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The tip or lower extremity of the tongue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's prepuce.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions concerning circumcision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The skin of the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical use recorded as an extended sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The core or innermost part of the heart; figuratively, one's deepest affection or sincerest agreement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The heart-expression carries both a literal anatomical image and idiomatic emotional or volitional meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small portion or quantity of cloud in the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wealth blessed with increase, or much and abundant wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of prosperous property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fruit-bearing or abounding in fruit, of a tree or land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a fruit-bearing tree or to land rich in fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full-moon night or a night with bright moonlight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression and lexical exception within the root's semantic family.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Perfect or complete in forbearance or clemency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison with ripe fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flower of the rose-coloured sorrel plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lubia or dolichos plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun distinct from the general fruit sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fruitful or productive intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression contrasting productive understanding with a barren intellect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abounding in wealth, of a people or company.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial or adjectival description of collective prosperity.

Adjectival counterpart of the butter-formation sense.

cautions: The wealth, gold-and-silver, and children/descendants senses for ثَمَر or ثَمَرَات are attributed Quranic interpretations alongside the ordinary fruit sense; the historical Lane citations have not been converted into modern verse keys unless independently supplied by QAC.
